facts.title: HCCL: Collective Communication for Meta Training and Inference Accelerators
facts.event_hint: Meta HCCL and MTIA 300 co-designed collective communication offload
facts.problem: Recommendation training and latency-sensitive inference are increasingly limited by collective communication, especially irregular AllToAllv, while conventional GPU-NIC stacks consume compute-grid resources and add host-device-NIC communication overhead.
facts.mechanism: MTIA 300 integrates backend networking on the chip package and provides dedicated message engines, near-memory compute, custom RDMA NIC IP, express doorbells, and asymmetric scale-up/scale-out links. HCCL compiles each collective into dependency-described subgraphs on the host, then dispatches them to message engines for autonomous execution. NMC performs reductions near memory, and inference paths use one-sided communication, device-resident/triggered collectives, and topology-aware selection to overlap communication with compute and bypass scheduling overhead.

evidence.claim: HCCL reaches up to 940 GB/s on intra-rack collectives while degrading concurrent compute throughput by less than 0.5%.
evidence.condition: MTIA 300 training collectives with overlapped computation and communication

evidence.claim: Inference-optimized collective paths achieve sub-6 microsecond collective latency.
MTIA 300's message engines and near-memory compute fully offload collective execution from the compute grid, enabling overlap with application computation.
evidence.baseline: Device compute-kernel execution used by libraries such as NCCL/RCCL
evidence.condition: Compiled HCCL subgraphs dispatched to dedicated message engines

evidence.claim: The accelerator package integrates network chiplets, RoCE IP, HBM3, and a high-bandwidth on-chip network instead of relying on a separate host-device-NIC path.
HCCL supports both training and inference optimizations, including parallel message-engine processing for bandwidth-bound collectives and one-sided primitives for latency-sensitive inference.
evidence.condition: Collective communication across MTIA 300's asymmetric scale-up/scale-out topology

facts.evaluation_context: The paper describes a library/hardware co-design for Meta's MTIA 300 accelerator, focused on ranking and recommendation workloads. It evaluates training collectives and latency-sensitive inference paths, reporting intra-rack bandwidth, overlap degradation, and inference collective latency; the excerpt does not give a general GPU baseline or production cluster size.
facts.limitations: Results are specific to MTIA 300's custom message engines, network package, HBM configuration, and Meta workloads; portability to GPU/NIC systems is not established by the excerpt. The reported 940 GB/s is an intra-rack collective peak rather than end-to-end model throughput, and sub-6µs is a collective-path metric rather than user-visible inference latency. Hardware integration, compiled-graph generation, topology-specific tuning, and dynamic QP management add deployment complexity (inference).
facts.project_relevance: For AI-infrastructure monitoring, HCCL shows a hardware path to make collective communication phase-aware and less dependent on compute-grid scheduling: reserve dedicated engines for communication, place reductions near memory, and expose one-sided low-latency paths for inference. Comparable evaluations should separate link/collective metrics from end-to-end model latency and quantify the cost of hardware-specific compilation and topology assumptions (inference).
